results.task: I have no pay yet this month. Rent is 900 and food is 300. Why do the percents of income not show? How are percents worked out?
results.reply:
Percents of income don't show because there is no income yet. A percent of income divides each spending line by total income, and dividing by zero isn't possible, so the script skips that part. Once you type your pay, the percents of income will appear.

The percents that did show are "share of spending." Each spending line's share is its part of total spending, so rent and food show 75% and 25% of your spending. Here is how the method works:

- Each line gets the whole-number part of its share, rounded down.
- Any points still missing are handed out one at a time to the lines with the largest leftover fractions. If lines tie, the one higher in your list gets the point.
- The shares of spending always add up to exactly 100, so the rounding never leaves a point missing or extra.

For percents of income, the same method runs with total income as the whole. Those percents add up to the share of your income that goes out, and they can total more than 100 when spending is more than income.

The script also shows that total spending is $1,200.00 and there is no income, so more goes out than comes in by $1,200.00. This only counts what you typed.
